zion-bic-abilene-ks.assessment: Zion BIC in Abilene is one of the founding Brethren in Christ congregations west of the Mississippi, organized in 1887 by River Brethren immigrants from Pennsylvania. The congregation has a notable missions-sending history within the BIC denomination, having produced numerous missionaries and church leaders. Pastor Jay Johnson currently leads, with Thomas Price as youth pastor. The 130-year heritage, plain Anabaptist roots, and small-town Kansas setting make this a meaningful spiritual home for those drawn to peace-church traditions. Yellow rating reflects the BIC denomination's allowance of female pastors, which the local Zion staff does not currently practice.

score_notes.mission: Zion has historically sent missionaries globally through BIC mission boards.

zion-opc-athens-tn.assessment: Zion Presbyterian Church is an Orthodox Presbyterian Church congregation in Athens, Tennessee, in the Presbytery of the Southeast. The OPC was founded in 1936 by J. Gresham Machen in defense of Reformed orthodoxy against theological liberalism — strict subscription to the Westminster Standards, male-only ordination, confessional accountability via presbytery, and Reformed expository preaching are denominational hallmarks. Rev. A. J. Millsaps serves as Pastor. For a man wanting confessional Reformed theology with the strictest US Presbyterian accountability, Zion OPC is a top-tier choice in east Tennessee.

zion-presbyterian-fredericksburg.assessment: Zion Presbyterian Church is one of the most theologically rigorous options in the Fredericksburg area. It is a congregation of the Free Church of Scotland (Continuing) — a denomination that holds to Biblical inerrancy and the original Westminster Confession of Faith without modification. This is not the touchy-feely mainline PCUSA Presbyterian; this is hard-core Westminster Calvinist confessionalism. Pastor Rom Prakashpalan is a converted Hindu/atheist who came to faith through hearing the Gospel (Romans 10:17), graduated RPTS with an MDiv, and was installed here in November 2024. The church is very new (2023) and meets at Fredericksburg Christian School. Two Sunday services (10:30 AM and 2:00 PM) plus a Thursday prayer meeting demonstrate seriousness. The lack of men's ministry is understandable for a plant this young. For a man who wants unapologetic Reformed confessionalism and a pastor with a powerful conversion testimony, this is a must-visit.
